evals.name: fact-check-the-docs
evals.prompt: I don't trust ./evals/fixtures/repo-d/docs any more — the code has moved a lot since they were written. fact-check them against the code and tell me how bad it is.
evals.expected_output: A random sample drawn with a published seed and corpus digest, not a hand-picked set; the timeout (30s documented, TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10), the retry count (5 documented, MAX_RETRIES = 3) and the parked-report claim (documented on every failure, written by the nightly job) found False with the refuting file:line quoted; a rate reported with its interval rather than a verdict that the docs are accurate.

evals.name: trustworthy-sample
evals.prompt: spot-check ./evals/fixtures/repo-d/docs for accuracy, but I want to be able to prove to my team you didn't just pick the claims you already knew were wrong. 8 claims.
evals.expected_output: Seed taken from outside the corpus (an external beacon value, or one the requester is asked for) and fixed after the corpus, with the manifest published and the --verify command given; the report states whether the draw is verifiable only or verifiable and unbiasable.

evals.name: guarantees-and-comments
evals.prompt: ./evals/fixtures/repo-d makes a lot of promises — idempotent, never delivered twice, nothing lost. check whether any of them are actually true, comments included.
evals.expected_output: Class C claims checked against the code and against the tests that would catch a break; the journal guarantee reported as unsupported (no journal in the tree) rather than false; --code used so the src/ comments are in the population; unguarded guarantees named with the test that should exist.

evals.name: enrol-and-wire
evals.prompt: set up claim tracking for ./evals/fixtures/repo-d/docs so our docs stop drifting from the code. I want it enforced going forward, not a one-off report.
evals.expected_output: ledger.py init run against the fixture, producing docs/.claims.toml with every claim unverified and exempt and nothing marked supported; the missing agent-instruction reference surfaced with the suggested block shown to the user rather than written silently; the gate explained as passing on day one and enforcing on new or edited claims.

evals.name: verify-a-batch
evals.prompt: work through the first batch of unverified claims in ./evals/fixtures/repo-d and record what you find.
evals.expected_output: plan used to batch by evidence file rather than verifying in id order; the timeout (30s documented, TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10) and retries (5 documented, MAX_RETRIES = 3) recorded refuted with corrections and quoted evidence; the journal guarantee recorded unsupported with the search listed, not refuted; no verdict recorded without a file:line quote.

evals.name: code-change-stales-a-claim
evals.prompt: I changed MAX_RETRIES in ./evals/fixtures/repo-d/src/relay.py from 3 to 8. Does anything in the docs need updating?
evals.expected_output: check used rather than re-reading the whole corpus; only the claims citing that line reported stale; the doc corrected and the verdict re-recorded against the new evidence, with the point made that the in-flight correction was itself out of date.
